items.item_text: Master’s Degree preferred

Command-level experience leading and managing a large and complex law enforcement workforce at a multi-site organization, ideally at a university and/or medical center, or similarly complex organization.

The Chief of Police (Chief) serves as the chief law enforcement and public safety executive for the University of California, Davis (UC Davis) and provides strategic leadership, direction, and oversight for all police and public safety operations.
Police Operations And Administration

The Chief is responsible for developing and implementing a comprehensive campus public safety program that supports the University's academic, research, residential, healthcare, and administrative missions while promoting a safe, inclusive, and welcoming environment for students, faculty, staff, visitors, and the broader university community.

Leads two full-service, 24/7/365 police operations on the Davis and Sacramento campuses of significant size and scale. Administers satellite security operations on both campuses for specialized and high-risk

Reporting to the Vice Chancellor, Finance, Operations and Administration (FOA) the Chief establishes the vision, priorities, policies, and operational strategies for the UC Davis Police Department. The Chief advises UC Davis executive leadership, including the Chancellor and UC Davis Health executives.

The position exercises broad authority and accountability for department operations, personnel, fiscal resources, emergency preparedness, crime prevention, investigations, police services, and strategic partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.

The Chief balances the University's educational mission and values with the responsibilities of a sworn law enforcement agency, exercising sound judgment in complex and often highly visible situations. The position also requires exceptional leadership, integrity, discretion, communication skills, and the ability to build trust across a diverse university community.
Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 11:59p PST; screening and selection can begin anytime.
Must be 21 years or older and a U.S. citizen.

Must possess a current California POST Management Certificate issued by the Commission on Peace Officers' Standards and Training, or ability to obtain this certificate within one year of appointment for out-of-state candidates.
Must posses a Class C California Drivers License or the ability to secure the same license quickly after hire. Must enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program.
Bachelor’s Degree in criminal justice, public or business administration, or similar discipline.
Achieved the rank of Captain or above, required.
Command level experience in leading and managing a law enforcement workforce.
Knowledge of criminal justice system with emphasis on the role of law enforcement as it relates to other agencies within the system, particularly prosecutors and the courts.
Knowledge of current police methods and procedures, including apprehension and arrest, criminal investigations, collection and presentation of evidence, and police record keeping.
Knowledge of police operating rules and regulations. Working knowledge of Peace Officers Bill of Rights (POBR). Knowledge of pertinent case law.
Skills to understand and interpret the rules and regulations of the Police Department, pertinent University and City ordinances and regulations, State and Federal laws and court decisions.
Oral and written communication skills to develop written narratives, reports, memoranda, correspondence, department policies, procedures and related material and convey them to a diverse community.
Decision making skills to conduct both routine and complex tasks that require knowledge of law, case law and personnel.

Organizational skills to achieve timely progress on multiple simultaneous complex projects, distribute effort appropriately among the projects, meet deadlines and maintain a high level of productivity.
Skills to use police equipment and law enforcement technology, including computer hardware and software, vehicles, firearms, and non-lethal weapons.
Knowledge to assess performance and communications skills to provide accurate and timely feedback, resolve problems/conflicts, and build effective team environment.
Skills to develop logical plans, evaluating alternatives and anticipating risks, obstacles, and likely consequences.
Skills to assess, prioritize, organize and direct others in major event planning or incident response.
Attendance at an advanced law enforcement executive leadership program, such as the FBI National Academy or the Senior Management Institute for Police preferred
